questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which acting company did Shakespeare belong to?
questions.why: Shakespeare was a member and shareholder of the Lord Chamberlain's Men, later renamed the King's Men. The other companies are invented names, not real Elizabethan troupes he belonged to.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What is it called when a character on stage reveals a hidden identity or feeling to the audience alone?
questions.why: An aside is a short remark a character makes directly to the audience, unheard by other characters. A soliloquy is longer and spoken alone on stage, not aimed at the audience mid-scene.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of sexual reproduction over asexual reproduction?
questions.why: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents, creating genetic variation that helps populations adapt. Asexual reproduction is faster but produces identical clones.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What replaced centralised Roman government in western Europe after Rome's fall?
questions.why: Power fragmented into local feudal lords controlling their own regions, rather than one central authority. There was no single elected or Byzantine ruler over western Europe.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In feudal society, what did a lord give a vassal in return for loyalty and service?
questions.why: Lords granted vassals land, called a fief, in exchange for military service and loyalty. This land-for-service bond was the core of the feudal relationship.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Romeo and Juliet, which line best captures the love vs hate theme through contradiction?
questions.why: This line pairs opposite ideas — love and hate — directly, showing how the two themes are tangled together. The other quotes are famous but don't combine the two opposites.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What payment did the medieval Church demand from ordinary people as a religious duty?
questions.why: Tithes were a portion of income, often a tenth, owed to the Church by ordinary people. Rents and tariffs were different kinds of payments unrelated to Church duty.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which Italian cities grew wealthy by transporting and supplying Crusader armies?
questions.why: Venice and Genoa built major trade wealth by shipping soldiers and supplies to the Holy Land during the Crusades. The other Italian cities were significant but not the main Crusade trade hubs.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Around what year was William Shakespeare born?
questions.why: Shakespeare was born in 1564 in Stratford-upon-Avon and died in 1616. 1601 and 1616 relate to his later works and death, not his birth.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What poetic rhythm does Shakespeare mainly use for dialogue in Romeo and Juliet?
questions.why: Shakespeare wrote most dialogue in iambic pentameter, a rhythm of ten alternating stressed and unstressed syllables. Rhyming couplets appear sometimes but aren't the main structure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Why do many flowering plants rely on insects or wind for pollination instead of self-pollinating?
questions.why: Cross-pollination mixes genetic material from different plants, increasing variation and helping offspring survive changing conditions. Self-pollination is easier but produces less varied offspring.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A classmate says the Crusades only matter for religious history and have nothing to do with economics. Using your own reasoning, explain how the Crusades affected trade and the wealth of specific regions.
